definitions.explanation: Vegetables grown primarily for their edible leaves, such as spinach, lettuce, cabbage, and komatsuna. A common category in grocery shopping and cooking.

examples.japanese: {葉物野菜|はものやさい}は{値段|ねだん}が{変|か}わりやすい。
examples.english: Leafy vegetables are prone to price fluctuations.

examples.japanese: {冬|ふゆ}は{葉物野菜|はものやさい}が{高|たか}くなることが{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Leafy vegetables often become expensive in winter.

examples.japanese: {葉物野菜|はものやさい}は{鮮度|せんど}が{落|お}ちやすいので、{早|はや}めに{使|つか}い{切|き}ったほうがいい。
examples.english: Leafy vegetables lose their freshness quickly, so it's better to use them up early.

notes:
USAGE:
A practical grocery and cooking term. Common {葉物野菜|はものやさい} include {小松菜|こまつな} (komatsuna), ほうれん{草|そう} (spinach), {白菜|はくさい} (Chinese cabbage), レタス (lettuce), and {春菊|しゅんぎく} (chrysanthemum greens).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {葉物野菜|はものやさい}を{買|か}う (to buy leafy vegetables)
- {葉物野菜|はものやさい}が{不足|ふそく}する (to be short on leafy vegetables)
- {新鮮|しんせん}な{葉物野菜|はものやさい} (fresh leafy vegetables)

RELATED WORDS:
- {根菜|こんさい} (root vegetables)
- {緑黄色野菜|りょくおうしょくやさい} (green and yellow vegetables)
